newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil coffee to continue to see mild temps - Somar.
newsitem.headline: Brazil coffee to continue to see mild temps - Somar.

text.p: Brazil's coffee regions will continue to see mild temperatures throughout this week with no threatening polar air mass forecast to enter coffee areas in the seven-day outlook, local meteorologists Somar said Sunday.
Minimum temperatures are forecast to continue between 11 and 16 degrees Celsius, said Somar forecaster Marcos Massari.
A cold front will pass through north Parana state on Monday, spreading to south Minas Gerais on Tuesday but will bring only scattered showers, he added.

The mild temperatures over the past few weeks have been attributed to the El Nino weather phenomenon which is developing in the Pacific Ocean and which is keeping all polar air masses to the far south of the country.
With no damaging cold forecast in the next seven days, the risk of frosts now in coffee areas this winter was slight, Massari said.
"Unless we have something in the first week of August, the chance of frost is very slim," Massari said.
